KEY MESSAGE 1...As of 2:30 MA EDT...Current sfc analysis shows 
a broad 1026 mb sfc high building over the region from the W/SW,
although some thin, high clouds associated with TC Isaias are 
streaming over southern areas, while a few lake effect clouds 
have been across the Capital District, Mohawk Valley, and 
southwestern ADKs earlier tonight with the lake moisture 
becoming trapped beneath a sharp low/mid-level inversion seen on
the 00z KALY sounding. Lowering inversion heights and weakening
winds should keep additional lake effect clouds closer to the 
lakeshore through the rest of the night, so even the areas that 
are running a little warmer than previously expected should 
still seep temps drop several more degrees between now and 
sunrise. Lows will generally be in the 30s to low 40s, with some
upper 20s possible in the ADKs. Some patchy river valley fog 
will be possible, as well as some frost where temps drop near or
below freezing tonight. However, for areas where the growing 
season is still ongoing, frost is expected to be too patchy to 
warrant frost advisory issuance. 

Large-scale subsidence is expected today as the sfc high remains 
overhead and strengthens beneath confluent upper flow on the 
poleward side of an amplifying upper ridge. After a cool start to 
the day, highs rise into the 50s to low 60s with calm winds and low 
humidity. Tonight, the sfc high will be close enough for temps to 
drop quite quickly after sunset, but temps should level off or 
even rise slightly towards sunrise as high clouds increase in 
coverage. NBM seems to have caught onto the radiative cooling 
trend, so only minor downward adjustments were needed with this 
forecast package. Lows again range from the 30s to low 40s, with
the coolest temps across northeastern areas tonight. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Isaias has mad landfall along the Gulf Coast as
a hurricane this evening. Its remnants are expected to track 
northwards into the region tomorrow. PWATs rise to around 1.3 - 
1.5" tomorrow into tomorrow night. The best low-level warm 
advection remains just south of our region, which is where the 
highest rainfall totals of around or just over an inch are 
expected. Some enhancement from the left exit region of an upper
jet streak is expected here as well. However, a band of mid-
level FGEN across the region and the right entrance of the upper
jet to our north will allow the precip shield to overspread our
entire CWA, with a quarter to half inch for our northernmost 
zones, with a half to 1" of rain for the rest of our area. Even 
if some locally higher amounts occur like the NAM suggests, 
flooding is still not expected given dry antecedent conditions 
and significantly weakened state of the sfc low as it tracks 
south of Long Island. This will be a very beneficial rain for 
the region.

There is still some uncertainty in just how quickly rain 
overspreads the region tomorrow, but southern areas should begin
to see rain develop by mid-morning, with rain reaching the I-90
corridor by mid- afternoon and finally our northeastern zones 
by sunset. Rain tapers off to showers Sunday night, with showers
generally ending by 12z Monday. Monday now looks mainly dry, 
with a narrow ridge of high pressure building over the area. 
Temps likely end up a few degrees above normal, mainly in the 
mid and upper 60s.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Tuesday into Tuesday night, a cold front looks to 
move through the region, bringing another chance for showers. 
We may briefly get into a warm sector Monday night into early 
Tuesday, but a wave of low pressure is expected to develop along
the frontal boundary to our north, helping push it 
southeastwards from southern Canada through our region Tuesday.
There remains some uncertainty in how close to our region the 
developing sfc low will track, but if it tracks to our north 
(which is the current consensus), then there could be enough 
instability for a few rumbles of thunder with the showers ahead
of the frontal passage. We dry out Wednesday and Thursday with 
sfc high pressure building overhead again. However, the pattern 
aloft does not look quite as amplified as it did a day or two 
ago. So, while it will cool down with temps a few degrees below 
normal, this cold shot does not look as impressive as noted in 
previous forecasts. Looking towards the end of the forecast 
period, we may begin to warm up towards the very end of the week
ahead of another storm system expected to track to our west 
next weekend.
